title: Gut Microbiome Diversity in Adults With Inflammatory and Immune-Mediated Skin Diseases
official: Studio Sulla diversità Del Microbiota Intestinale Umano in Pazienti Con Patologie Infiammatorie Cutanee
summary:
This study will examine whether the gut bacteria of adults with inflammatory or immune-mediated skin diseases differ from those of healthy adults. It will include people with atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa, vitiligo, alopecia areata, acne, pemphigus, or bullous pemphigoid, as well as healthy controls.

Participants will provide a stool sample and complete a short food diary. The study team will analyze the bacteria in the samples and compare the results between the disease groups and healthy controls. Participants with a skin disease will be asked to provide a second stool sample and complete follow-up assessments about six months later; healthy controls will provide one sample. The study will also examine whether changes in gut bacteria are related to skin disease severity, diet, and other collected health information.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older.
* Able and willing to provide informed consent.
* For patient groups: specialist-confirmed diagnosis of atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa, vitiligo, alopecia areata, acne, pemphigus, or bullous pemphigoid.
* For healthy controls: no diagnosis of the skin diseases studied.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Unable to provide informed consent or complete the study procedures.
* Systemic antibiotic treatment within 8 weeks before recruitment or during follow-up.
* Previous intestinal surgery.
* Inflammatory bowel disease, constipation, or diarrhea.
* Long-term alcohol use.
